note: Review-only companion; not a TestsData row. Keys include rationales. This is an educational syllabus bank, not legal advice; confirm any law/current institutional detail against the Constitution and relevant official sources before production use.

questions.text: On which date was the Constitution of India adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
questions.rationale: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949.

questions.text: When did the Constitution of India come into force?
questions.rationale: It came into force on 26 January 1950.

questions.text: Who chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
questions.rationale: B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.

questions.text: Which opening words introduce the Preamble?
questions.rationale: The Preamble begins with “We, the people of India”.

questions.text: Which set contains the four ideals expressly stated in the Preamble?
questions.rationale: The Preamble describes justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.

questions.text: Which amendment added the words Socialist, Secular and Integrity to the Preamble?
questions.rationale: The 42nd Amendment of 1976 added those terms.

questions.text: India is described in the Preamble as a:
questions.rationale: That is the Preamble's description of India.

questions.text: Which body framed and adopted the Constitution before it came into force?
questions.rationale: The Constituent Assembly framed and adopted the Constitution.

questions.text: Which concept means that public power is exercised under and limited by the Constitution?
questions.rationale: Constitutionalism emphasizes limited government under constitutional rules.

questions.text: Which statement best describes a written constitution?

options.label: A
options.text: It is identical to every ordinary statute

options.label: B
options.text: Its principal rules are set out in a formal written document

options.label: C
options.text: Its rules exist only in uncodified custom

questions.rationale: A written constitution formally sets out constitutional provisions.

questions.text: Fundamental Rights are primarily contained in which Part of the Constitution?
questions.rationale: Part III contains Fundamental Rights.

questions.text: Which Article guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws?
questions.rationale: Article 14 addresses equality before the law and equal protection.

questions.text: Article 19 protects specified freedoms of:
questions.rationale: Article 19 grants specified freedoms to citizens, with permissible restrictions.

questions.text: Article 21 protects which right?

options.label: A
options.text: Life and personal liberty, except according to procedure established by law

options.label: B
options.text: Only the right to own a business

options.label: D
options.text: Only the right to receive public employment

questions.rationale: Article 21 protects life and personal liberty.

questions.text: Directive Principles of State Policy are found in:
questions.rationale: Part IV contains the Directive Principles.

questions.text: Which statement best describes Directive Principles?

options.label: A
options.text: They guide the State in governance but are not directly enforceable by courts in the same manner as Fundamental Rights

options.label: B
options.text: They are criminal penalties in every case

options.label: D
options.text: They apply only to private companies

questions.rationale: Article 37 says Directive Principles are not enforceable by courts but are fundamental in governance.

questions.text: Fundamental Duties are mainly listed in:
questions.rationale: Part IVA contains Fundamental Duties.

questions.text: Which Article lists Fundamental Duties?
questions.rationale: Article 51A lists citizens' Fundamental Duties.

questions.text: Which amendment inserted Fundamental Duties into the Constitution?
questions.rationale: The 42nd Amendment inserted Part IVA and Article 51A.

questions.text: Which of the following is a Fundamental Duty?

options.label: A
options.text: To disregard public property during protests

options.label: B
options.text: To treat every personal preference as law

options.label: C
options.text: To protect and improve the natural environment

questions.rationale: Article 51A includes protecting and improving the natural environment.

questions.text: Who is the constitutional head of the Union executive?
questions.rationale: The President is the constitutional head of the Union executive.

questions.text: Who normally leads the Union Council of Ministers and government?
questions.rationale: The Prime Minister leads the Council of Ministers.

questions.text: The Parliament of India consists of:
questions.rationale: Parliament comprises the President, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.

questions.text: Which House is directly elected by eligible voters in general elections?
questions.rationale: Lok Sabha members are directly elected from territorial constituencies.

questions.text: Which statement about Rajya Sabha is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a body of State Governors

options.label: B
options.text: It is dissolved after every general election

options.label: C
options.text: Its members are all directly elected by the whole country

options.label: D
options.text: It is a permanent House and is not subject to dissolution

questions.rationale: Rajya Sabha is a continuing House.

questions.text: Who formally appoints the Prime Minister?
questions.rationale: The President appoints the Prime Minister, conventionally the person able to command Lok Sabha confidence.

questions.text: The Union Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to:
questions.rationale: Article 75(3) provides collective responsibility to Lok Sabha.

questions.text: Which House is often called the House of the People?
questions.rationale: Lok Sabha is the House of the People.

questions.text: Who presides over proceedings of Lok Sabha?
questions.rationale: The Speaker presides over Lok Sabha.

questions.text: Which institution is the highest judicial authority in India?
questions.rationale: The Supreme Court is the apex court.

questions.text: Who is the constitutional head of a state in India?
questions.rationale: The Governor is the constitutional head of the state.

questions.text: Who normally heads the elected state government?
questions.rationale: The Chief Minister leads the state Council of Ministers.

questions.text: Who appoints a State Governor?
questions.rationale: The President appoints the Governor.

questions.text: Which body is chiefly associated with urban local self-government in a large city?
questions.rationale: Municipal corporations are urban local-government bodies.

questions.text: Which body is a district-level rural local-government institution?
questions.rationale: Zila Panchayat functions at district level in the rural local-government structure.

questions.text: Which constitutional Article vests superintendence, direction and control of specified elections in the Election Commission of India?
questions.rationale: Article 324 concerns the Election Commission of India.

questions.text: The State Election Commission is associated with elections to:

options.label: B
options.text: Only the offices of President and Vice-President

options.label: D
options.text: Panchayats and Municipalities in the State

questions.rationale: State Election Commissions supervise local-body elections under the relevant constitutional provisions.

questions.text: Which amendment constitutionalized the Panchayati Raj framework?
questions.rationale: The 73rd Amendment added the Panchayat provisions.

questions.text: Which amendment constitutionalized the municipalities framework?
questions.rationale: The 74th Amendment added Part IXA on municipalities.

questions.text: Which official commonly coordinates district-level administration for the State government?

options.label: A
options.text: District Collector/District Magistrate, depending on the state structure

questions.rationale: District administration commonly operates through the Collector/District Magistrate and related officers.

questions.text: A public authority refuses the same legal protection to two people in materially identical circumstances without a relevant reason. Which constitutional principle is most directly raised?

options.label: A
options.text: Equality before law and equal protection under Article 14

options.label: B
options.text: Freedom of speech under Article 19 only

questions.rationale: Article 14 addresses equality before law and equal protection.

questions.text: A citizen's speech is restricted by a law. Which is the most accurate way to evaluate the restriction under Article 19?

options.label: A
options.text: Article 19 permits no restrictions in any circumstances

options.label: B
options.text: Check the relevant freedom and whether the restriction fits a constitutionally permitted ground and is reasonable

options.label: C
options.text: Treat Article 19 as a duty rather than a right

questions.rationale: Article 19 freedoms are subject to specified constitutional restrictions.

questions.text: A government policy promotes public health but a person argues it is a Directive Principle. Which statement best distinguishes its legal status from a Fundamental Right?

options.label: A
options.text: Every Directive Principle is an offence provision

options.label: B
options.text: Directive Principles always override every Fundamental Right

options.label: C
options.text: A Directive Principle guides state policy but is not directly enforceable in the same way as a Fundamental Right

options.label: D
options.text: Directive Principles apply only to citizens' private conduct

questions.rationale: Directive Principles guide governance and are non-justiciable under Article 37.

questions.text: A person challenges a deprivation of personal liberty. Which Article is most directly relevant to the stated syllabus?
questions.rationale: Article 21 protects life and personal liberty.

questions.text: A student says Fundamental Duties and Fundamental Rights are identical because both appear in the Constitution. Which correction is strongest?

options.label: A
options.text: Rights are found only in Part IV

options.label: B
options.text: Fundamental Rights are enforceable rights in Part III; Fundamental Duties are listed for citizens in Part IVA

options.label: C
options.text: Both sets apply only to the President

options.label: D
options.text: Duties are found only in local bylaws

questions.rationale: The two sets have different roles, placement and legal character.

questions.text: A policy objective appears in Part IV, but a petitioner wants a court order solely to enforce it as a Directive Principle. Which constitutional statement is most relevant?

options.label: A
options.text: Part IV applies only during elections

options.label: B
options.text: Part IV is the same as Part III

options.label: C
options.text: All policies in Part IV are criminal provisions

options.label: D
options.text: Article 37 states Directive Principles are not enforceable by courts, while remaining fundamental in governance

questions.rationale: Article 37 provides the relevant non-justiciability rule.

questions.text: An amendment changes a constitutional provision but is challenged for damaging the Constitution's basic structure. Which doctrine is most relevant?
questions.rationale: The basic structure doctrine limits the amending power.

questions.text: A district officer administers relief in the district and coordinates local departments. Which syllabus topic is most directly illustrated?

options.label: A
options.text: State election of Rajya Sabha members

questions.rationale: District administration concerns coordination and implementation at district level.

questions.text: A city council handles local services, while rural district local affairs are handled through a Zila Panchayat. Which distinction is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Municipal Corporation is the national election authority

options.label: C
options.text: Zila Panchayat administers the Union Cabinet

options.label: D
options.text: Municipal Corporation is urban local government; Zila Panchayat is rural local government at district level

questions.rationale: These institutions serve different local-government contexts.

questions.text: A general election to the Lok Sabha is being conducted, and a separate city municipal election is scheduled. Which bodies have the respective constitutional roles?

options.label: A
options.text: State Election Commission conducts both in every case

options.label: B
options.text: Election Commission of India for Lok Sabha; State Election Commission for municipal elections

questions.rationale: ECI handles parliamentary elections; State EC handles municipal and Panchayat elections.

questions.text: The Prime Minister's Council of Ministers loses a confidence vote in Lok Sabha. Which constitutional principle is most directly implicated?

options.label: B
options.text: Collective responsibility of the Union Council of Ministers to Lok Sabha

options.label: C
options.text: The independence of the State Election Commission

questions.rationale: The Union Council is collectively responsible to Lok Sabha.

questions.text: A student calls the President the day-to-day political head of the elected Union government. Which correction is best?

options.label: A
options.text: The Chief Election Commissioner leads the Council of Ministers

options.label: B
options.text: The Chief Justice is day-to-day executive head

options.label: C
options.text: The Prime Minister leads the government while the President is the constitutional head

options.label: D
options.text: The Speaker runs the Union ministries

questions.rationale: The PM leads the government; the President is constitutional head.

questions.text: A proposal is passed only by Lok Sabha, but the student claims it has therefore been passed by Parliament in every case. What must be considered?

options.label: B
options.text: The state Governor's personal preference only

options.label: D
options.text: The Constitution's lawmaking procedure and whether Rajya Sabha's participation is required for that measure

questions.rationale: Parliament generally comprises both Houses and the President, with procedures varying by measure.

questions.text: A Governor receives advice from a state's Council of Ministers for ordinary state executive business. Which official is the normal political head of that Council?
questions.rationale: The Chief Minister heads the state Council of Ministers.

questions.text: A person argues that a Fundamental Right can never be limited. Which response best fits the course topics?

options.label: A
options.text: Part III contains only non-binding policy aims

options.label: B
options.text: All Fundamental Rights can be cancelled by an ordinary officer

options.label: C
options.text: Some rights, including Article 19 freedoms, are subject to constitutionally specified restrictions

options.label: D
options.text: Article 21 applies only to elected legislators

questions.rationale: Article 19 explicitly allows specified restrictions.

questions.text: A state makes policy to improve public health and welfare. Which constitutional part is especially relevant as guiding principles for State policy?
questions.rationale: Directive Principles are in Part IV.

questions.text: A citizen damages public property during a protest. Which Fundamental Duty is most directly relevant to the conduct?

options.label: A
options.text: Duty to vote in every election as stated in Article 51A

options.label: B
options.text: Duty to safeguard public property and abjure violence

options.label: C
options.text: Duty to serve as a judge

options.label: D
options.text: Duty to protect the environment only

questions.rationale: Article 51A includes safeguarding public property and abjuring violence.

questions.text: A teacher is describing an amendment's constitutional history. Which pair is correct?

options.label: B
options.text: 42nd Amendment inserted the right to property as a Fundamental Right; 73rd created Rajya Sabha

options.label: D
options.text: 42nd inserted Fundamental Duties; 86th added the duty of a parent/guardian to provide educational opportunities for children aged 6–14

questions.rationale: The 42nd Amendment inserted Part IVA; the 86th Amendment added clause 51A(k).

questions.text: A State Election Commission plans local-body elections, but a student says Article 324 alone assigns the ECI all elections of every kind. Which correction is best?

options.label: A
options.text: The Constitution separately provides for State Election Commissions for Panchayat and municipal elections

options.label: B
options.text: All elections are conducted by municipal commissioners

options.label: C
options.text: Article 324 deals only with school elections

options.label: D
options.text: Local elections are not constitutionally addressed

questions.rationale: Local-body elections are assigned to State Election Commissions under Part IX/IXA provisions.

questions.text: A local body has been asked to handle city-level services rather than district rural planning. Which institution is a better fit?
questions.rationale: A municipal corporation is an urban local-government institution.

questions.text: A law treats a person differently based solely on an arbitrary classification unrelated to its purpose. Which constitutional concern is most directly raised?

options.label: A
options.text: The definition of a Municipal Corporation

questions.rationale: Article 14 is relevant to arbitrary state action and unequal legal treatment.

questions.text: A citizen seeks to challenge restrictions on peaceful expression. What must a constitutional analysis identify before judging validity?

options.label: A
options.text: Only whether a government official signed the notice

options.label: B
options.text: Only whether the person lives in a city

options.label: C
options.text: The name of the local municipal ward

options.label: D
options.text: The relevant Article 19 freedom, the restriction's purpose and whether it meets the constitutional test

questions.rationale: Restrictions must be assessed against the specific freedom and permitted grounds.

questions.text: A policy objective is listed as a Directive Principle and is consistent with a Fundamental Right. Which approach best reflects the Constitution's framework?

options.label: A
options.text: Read the provisions harmoniously, recognizing Part IV's guidance and Part III's enforceable rights

options.label: B
options.text: Treat Directive Principles as automatically unenforceable in every policy decision

options.label: C
options.text: Use Part IV as the sole source of criminal offences

questions.rationale: Directive Principles guide policy and should be considered with Fundamental Rights.

questions.text: An official detains a person and relies only on a personal preference, without lawful authority or procedure. Which provision is most directly engaged?

options.label: B
options.text: Article 21 protection of life and personal liberty

options.label: C
options.text: Article 14 only in every possible case

questions.rationale: Article 21 is directly related to life and personal liberty.

questions.text: The Constitution's Preamble is invoked to interpret an ambiguous provision. Which description best fits its role?

options.label: A
options.text: A separate criminal code replacing all Articles

options.label: C
options.text: A source of unrestricted executive power

options.label: D
options.text: A useful aid expressing constitutional objectives and values, read with the text rather than replacing it

questions.rationale: The Preamble expresses values and can aid interpretation but does not replace the Constitution's operative provisions.

questions.text: An amendment is challenged as destroying a foundational feature such as constitutional supremacy. Which case-law doctrine is relevant to the course's basic-structure topic?
questions.rationale: The basic structure doctrine addresses limits on constitutional amendments.

questions.text: A student says that because the Constitution is written, every rule must appear in one unamended original document. Which correction is best?

options.label: A
options.text: Amendments automatically replace all Fundamental Rights

options.label: C
options.text: Written constitutions can be amended according to their prescribed procedures

options.label: D
options.text: Only Governors can amend the Constitution

questions.rationale: Written constitutions can provide formal amendment procedures.

questions.text: A bill concerning ordinary Union governance is being studied. Which distinction between Parliament and the executive is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Parliament is the Union legislature; the Council of Ministers is part of the executive

options.label: B
options.text: The Supreme Court is one of Parliament's Houses

options.label: C
options.text: The Election Commission debates and enacts all laws

options.label: D
options.text: The Governor presides over both Houses of Parliament

questions.rationale: Parliament legislates; the Council of Ministers performs executive functions.

questions.text: A state policy initiative is overseen by a Chief Minister and ministers, while the Governor remains constitutional head. Which statement is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: The district Collector heads the state legislature

options.label: B
options.text: The Governor is the constitutional head; the Chief Minister leads the elected government

options.label: C
options.text: The State Election Commissioner leads all state departments

options.label: D
options.text: The Chief Minister is the constitutional head and Governor is the elected head

questions.rationale: That distinction reflects the parliamentary state executive.

questions.text: A city's municipal poll date is announced. A student asks whether the ECI or State EC is normally constitutionally responsible. Which is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The Zila Panchayat itself for all cities

options.label: B
options.text: The Supreme Court as election organizer

options.label: D
options.text: State Election Commission, under the constitutional local-body election framework

questions.rationale: State Election Commissions supervise Panchayat and municipal elections.

questions.text: A school textbook says Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution through an amendment. Which pairing is correct?
questions.rationale: The 42nd Amendment introduced Part IVA and Article 51A.

questions.text: A parent or guardian is asked which Fundamental Duty concerns children's education. Which is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: Article 51A(k) addresses providing educational opportunities to a child/ward aged 6–14

options.label: B
options.text: Article 19 requires free university education in every case

options.label: D
options.text: Article 14 requires every parent to be a teacher

questions.rationale: Article 51A(k) is the Fundamental Duty; Article 21A is the related right to education.

questions.text: A policy proposal concerns village-level elected self-government. Which amendment is most directly connected with the Panchayat framework?
questions.rationale: The 73rd Amendment concerns Panchayats.

questions.text: A municipality's constitutional framework is being discussed. Which Part was added for urban local bodies by the 74th Amendment?
questions.rationale: Part IXA addresses municipalities.

questions.text: A student confuses the Chief Election Commissioner with the State Election Commissioner. Which distinction is most accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: The ECI handles Parliament and State Legislature elections; State ECs handle Panchayat and municipal elections

options.label: B
options.text: The Chief Election Commissioner runs municipal elections in each city directly

options.label: C
options.text: The State EC appoints the President

options.label: D
options.text: Both are the same officer under all circumstances

questions.rationale: The constitutional remit differs between ECI and State Election Commissions.

questions.text: Which statement best describes the ECI's constitutional role?

options.label: C
options.text: It supervises specified electoral rolls and elections under Article 324

questions.rationale: Article 324 vests specified election superintendence, direction and control in the ECI.

questions.text: A person argues that the Constitution exists only to empower the government. Which Preamble value most clearly contradicts an unlimited-power view?

options.label: C
options.text: Unlimited terms for every elected body

options.label: D
options.text: Justice, liberty, equality and fraternity as constitutional objectives

questions.rationale: The Preamble states values including justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.

questions.text: A public authority treats people unequally and also restricts a citizen's speech. Which two provisions are the most direct starting points for analysis?
questions.rationale: Article 14 concerns equality; Article 19 covers specified freedoms.

questions.text: A legal complaint concerns both an arbitrary procedure affecting liberty and unequal treatment under law. Which Articles are most directly relevant?
questions.rationale: Article 14 addresses equality and Article 21 protects life and personal liberty.

questions.text: A district administration office is implementing state policy and coordinating local public services. Which level is most directly represented?

options.label: C
options.text: Municipal Corporation only in every case

questions.rationale: District administration coordinates government functions at district level.

questions.text: A law restricts a citizen's speech to address a public concern. The citizen argues Article 19 makes all restrictions invalid. Which reasoning is most defensible?

options.label: A
options.text: Identify the relevant Article 19 freedom and test whether the restriction is reasonable and falls within a constitutionally permitted ground

options.label: B
options.text: Treat the restriction as a Fundamental Duty

options.label: C
options.text: Decide solely by the location of the person's district

options.label: D
options.text: Declare every speech restriction invalid without examining the provision

questions.rationale: Article 19 freedoms are not unlimited; constitutional grounds and reasonableness matter.

questions.text: An amendment changes an institution in a way alleged to eliminate judicial review and constitutional limits. Which framework most directly addresses whether a constitutional amendment can destroy foundational features?

options.label: A
options.text: The ordinary rule for email notices

questions.rationale: The basic structure doctrine constrains constitutional amendments that damage basic features.

questions.text: A government scheme promotes social welfare, but its implementation treats similarly situated citizens arbitrarily. Which constitutional analysis is strongest?

options.label: A
options.text: Directive Principles automatically excuse unequal treatment

options.label: B
options.text: Only Article 324 applies to all government actions

options.label: C
options.text: Consider Part IV's policy objective while separately testing implementation under Article 14 and relevant rights

options.label: D
options.text: A welfare purpose removes the need for legal authority

questions.rationale: A policy goal does not remove applicable constitutional limits on state action.

questions.text: A person challenges a deprivation of liberty and an arbitrary classification used to justify it. Which pair of Articles provides the most direct starting points?
questions.rationale: Article 14 addresses equality; Article 21 concerns life and personal liberty.

questions.text: A student argues that the Preamble itself grants an unlimited legal power to an executive agency. What is the key flaw?

options.label: A
options.text: The Preamble is the same as Article 51A

options.label: B
options.text: The Preamble expresses constitutional values and aids interpretation; it does not independently grant unlimited executive authority

options.label: C
options.text: The Preamble overrides all operative Articles

options.label: D
options.text: Only the Preamble sets out local election procedures

questions.rationale: The Preamble must be read with the operative constitutional text.

questions.text: A legislature enacts a law, and the executive implements it. A student claims the Election Commission is a third lawmaking House. Which correction is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The ECI replaces Rajya Sabha in election years

options.label: B
options.text: The ECI is the court of final appeal in every dispute

options.label: C
options.text: The ECI is the Union Council of Ministers

options.label: D
options.text: The ECI is a constitutional election authority, not a House of Parliament

questions.rationale: The ECI has defined election functions; it is not part of Parliament's two Houses.

questions.text: A city municipal election and a Lok Sabha general election are both due. Which allocation matches the Constitution's institutional design?

options.label: A
options.text: ECI handles Lok Sabha; State Election Commission handles the municipal poll

options.label: B
options.text: Rajya Sabha runs municipal polls; ECI runs Lok Sabha poll

questions.rationale: The ECI and State EC have distinct electoral responsibilities.

questions.text: The Council of Ministers remains in office despite losing Lok Sabha confidence, and the executive refuses to account to the House. Which principle is most directly implicated?

options.label: B
options.text: The Preamble's wording about fraternity only

options.label: C
options.text: Collective responsibility of the Union Council of Ministers to Lok Sabha

options.label: D
options.text: Fundamental Duty to protect the environment

questions.rationale: Collective responsibility is a central feature of the parliamentary system.

questions.text: An official says Article 14 guarantees identical treatment even where relevant circumstances differ. Which statement is more accurate?

options.label: C
options.text: Article 14 applies only to elected officials

options.label: D
options.text: Equality requires equal protection and bars arbitrary discrimination, but reasonable classification may be constitutionally permitted

questions.rationale: Article 14 permits constitutionally reasonable classification rather than arbitrary unequal treatment.

questions.text: A Fundamental Right is asserted against a policy goal in Part IV. Which reading method best reflects the constitutional relationship?

options.label: A
options.text: Treat Directive Principles as criminal offences

options.label: B
options.text: Read the provisions harmoniously, recognizing enforceable rights and the directive role of Part IV

options.label: C
options.text: Assume both Parts have identical justiciability

questions.rationale: Part III and Part IV are read harmoniously, with distinct legal status.

questions.text: A claimant argues that because a policy appears in Part IV, courts must enforce it as if it were a Fundamental Right. Which constitutional text most directly challenges that claim?
questions.rationale: Article 37 says Directive Principles are not enforceable by courts.

questions.text: A law makes an unequal classification. The government explains a legitimate aim, but the classification has no rational connection to that aim. Which issue remains?

options.label: A
options.text: Whether it was published in a newspaper

options.label: B
options.text: Whether the Governor attended a meeting

options.label: C
options.text: Whether the classification meets Article 14's equality/non-arbitrariness requirements

options.label: D
options.text: Whether a municipal ward has been renumbered

questions.rationale: A legitimate objective alone does not cure an arbitrary or unrelated classification.

questions.text: A person is denied personal liberty under an executive order with no lawful procedure. The authority says that administrative convenience is sufficient. Which response best reflects Article 21?

options.label: B
options.text: Article 21 concerns only the right to vote

options.label: D
options.text: Personal liberty cannot be deprived except according to procedure established by law

questions.rationale: Article 21 expressly protects life and personal liberty subject to law.

questions.text: An amendment is challenged as abolishing the essential democratic character of the Constitution. Which sequence of analysis is most appropriate for a course-level answer?

options.label: A
options.text: Identify the alleged basic feature and assess it under the basic structure doctrine

options.label: B
options.text: Treat every amendment as automatically invalid

options.label: C
options.text: Check only whether the amendment title contains the word democratic

options.label: D
options.text: Ask the municipal corporation to ratify the amendment

questions.rationale: A basic-structure analysis identifies the feature and evaluates the amendment's effect.

questions.text: The Preamble's words 'Secular' and 'Socialist' were inserted by an amendment. Which statement about that history is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: They were included only by the 86th Amendment

options.label: B
options.text: They were added to the original text in 1947

options.label: C
options.text: They were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976

options.label: D
options.text: They are found only in Article 324

questions.rationale: The 42nd Amendment inserted Socialist and Secular into the Preamble.

questions.text: A Fundamental Duty to protect the environment is cited to automatically deny a person's otherwise lawful speech. Which conclusion is most careful?

options.label: A
options.text: The duty is relevant, but a restriction on speech must still be assessed under the constitutional provisions governing that freedom

options.label: B
options.text: Environmental protection is not mentioned in Article 51A

options.label: C
options.text: Article 51A applies only to municipal officers

options.label: D
options.text: Fundamental Duties automatically override every right

questions.rationale: A duty is relevant to constitutional values but does not replace the Article 19 analysis.

questions.text: A new state policy is consistent with a Directive Principle but is implemented in a way that violates Article 21. What follows?

options.label: A
options.text: Only Parliament's Speaker can evaluate it

options.label: B
options.text: Its policy objective alone does not eliminate the need to comply with applicable Fundamental Rights

options.label: C
options.text: Part IV automatically overrides Part III

options.label: D
options.text: Article 21 does not apply to government action

questions.rationale: Directive Principles guide governance; implementation must still respect applicable rights.

questions.text: A state Governor and a Chief Minister disagree about the ordinary political direction of a state government. Which principle best describes their normal roles?

options.label: A
options.text: The Governor is the elected day-to-day political leader

options.label: B
options.text: The Chief Minister is appointed by the municipal corporation

options.label: C
options.text: The District Collector is the constitutional head of the state

options.label: D
options.text: The Governor is constitutional head while the Chief Minister leads the elected government and Council of Ministers

questions.rationale: This is the basic distinction in the parliamentary state executive.

questions.text: A city and a rural district are designing local institutions. Which pairing is most consistent with the syllabus?

options.label: A
options.text: Municipal Corporation—urban local government; Zila Panchayat—district-level rural local government

options.label: C
options.text: Zila Panchayat—House of Parliament; Municipal Corporation—state Cabinet

options.label: D
options.text: Municipal Corporation—rural district; Zila Panchayat—Union legislature

questions.rationale: These are distinct local-government bodies for urban and rural contexts.

questions.text: A student says the ECI is responsible for every municipal poll because Article 324 covers elections. What is the best correction?

options.label: A
options.text: No constitutional body administers local elections

options.label: C
options.text: The Constitution separately provides State Election Commissions for Panchayat and municipal elections

options.label: D
options.text: Municipal polls are run by Lok Sabha

questions.rationale: The local-body framework separately provides for State Election Commissions.

questions.text: A law classifies citizens by a criterion unrelated to its stated goal; affected people also claim the criterion burdens an Article 19 freedom. What is the strongest analytical approach?

options.label: A
options.text: Assume a single Article automatically decides all claims

options.label: B
options.text: Treat the matter only as a Fundamental Duty

options.label: C
options.text: Assess equality/non-arbitrariness under Article 14 and separately test any Article 19 restriction against its applicable constitutional grounds

options.label: D
options.text: Refer the policy to a Zila Panchayat for constitutional interpretation

questions.rationale: Articles 14 and 19 address distinct but potentially overlapping constitutional questions.

questions.text: An administrator relies on an environmental duty to justify all restrictions on a public meeting. What should a balanced legal analysis do?

options.label: A
options.text: Treat Article 51A as the only enforceable right

options.label: B
options.text: Assume public meetings are always prohibited

options.label: C
options.text: Reject environmental protection as a constitutional concern

options.label: D
options.text: Recognize Article 51A's environmental duty but independently assess the restriction under the applicable rights and lawful procedure

questions.rationale: A constitutional duty does not automatically settle the validity of a rights restriction.

questions.text: A constitutional amendment changes the composition of a body, and challengers claim the change damages separation of powers and judicial review. What evidence is most important to the basic-structure question?

options.label: A
options.text: The amendment's actual legal effects on the alleged foundational features, considered under the basic-structure doctrine

options.label: B
options.text: Whether the amendment uses formal language

options.label: C
options.text: Whether a state Governor publicly supports the amendment

questions.rationale: The doctrine focuses on impact on basic constitutional features, not labels.

questions.text: A welfare scheme relies on a Directive Principle and denies a benefit through an arbitrary process. What is the most accurate conclusion?

options.label: A
options.text: Because welfare is a goal, all procedures are valid

options.label: B
options.text: The scheme's objective may be relevant, but its arbitrary implementation can still raise Article 14 concerns

options.label: C
options.text: Directive Principles are meaningless and must be ignored

options.label: D
options.text: The denial can never be reviewed

questions.rationale: A valid policy goal does not immunize arbitrary implementation.

questions.text: A citizen challenges an order affecting personal liberty. The authority claims Article 21 only applies when a law is completely absent, not when procedure exists but is arbitrary. Which response best reflects modern constitutional reasoning at course level?

options.label: B
options.text: Article 14 and 21 cannot ever be considered together

options.label: C
options.text: Any written procedure automatically validates every deprivation

options.label: D
options.text: Article 21 protection includes scrutiny of the legal procedure affecting life and liberty; the existence of a procedure alone does not end analysis

questions.rationale: Article 21 is not reduced to a bare existence of procedure; fairness and legality can matter.

questions.text: An interpretation dispute involves an ambiguous provision. One interpretation better advances justice, liberty and equality while remaining consistent with the text. How may the Preamble be used?

options.label: B
options.text: As an interpretive aid that illuminates constitutional objectives while the provision's text remains controlling

options.label: C
options.text: As an authority to disregard the operative text

options.label: D
options.text: As a substitute for all judicial reasoning

questions.rationale: The Preamble assists interpretation but does not displace operative provisions.

questions.text: The Union government loses Lok Sabha confidence but claims the Council of Ministers answers only to Rajya Sabha. Which constitutional feature refutes the claim?

options.label: A
options.text: The President presides over Rajya Sabha daily

options.label: D
options.text: The State Election Commission's municipal remit

questions.rationale: The Union Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to Lok Sabha.

questions.text: An election dispute concerns a Lok Sabha constituency, while a separate dispute concerns a municipal ward poll. Which institutional distinction is relevant at the outset?

options.label: A
options.text: ECI administers the parliamentary election; State EC administers municipal elections under the local-body framework

options.label: B
options.text: Both are conducted only by the Supreme Court

options.label: D
options.text: Both are necessarily conducted by Municipal Corporation itself

questions.rationale: The two types of elections fall under different constitutional election authorities.

questions.text: A person says all Directive Principles are individually enforceable in court because they are 'fundamental in governance'. Which reasoning corrects the conflation?

options.label: A
options.text: Only the President can decide enforceability

options.label: B
options.text: Article 37 expressly distinguishes their governance importance from direct court enforceability

options.label: C
options.text: Part IV is actually Part III

questions.rationale: Article 37 states both their importance and non-justiciability.

questions.text: A government claims equal protection demands the same outcome for every person regardless of materially relevant differences. What response is more accurate?

options.label: B
options.text: Article 14 only applies to local elections

options.label: C
options.text: Article 14 overrides every other provision automatically

options.label: D
options.text: Equal protection allows reasonable classification but not arbitrary discrimination

questions.rationale: Equality under Article 14 does not prohibit every classification; the classification must be constitutionally reasonable.

questions.text: A law limits a citizen's expression, uses a classification that may be arbitrary, and is defended as advancing a public-policy objective. Which review sequence is most defensible?

options.label: A
options.text: Review only the Preamble, ignoring the Articles

options.label: B
options.text: Apply Article 324 because every public dispute is electoral

options.label: C
options.text: Accept the objective as conclusive and stop

options.label: D
options.text: Examine the relevant Article 19 ground/reasonableness, assess the classification under Article 14, and consider the policy objective without treating it as a complete defence

questions.rationale: The issues require separate but coordinated analysis under rights provisions.

questions.text: A parent fails to provide educational opportunities to a child aged 8. Which pair most accurately separates a Fundamental Duty from the related right?

options.label: A
options.text: Article 51A(k) states the parental/guardian duty; Article 21A concerns the right to education for ages 6–14

options.label: C
options.text: Article 14 is the duty and Article 19 is the right

options.label: D
options.text: Article 324 is the duty and Article 51A is a right

questions.rationale: The duty and right have different constitutional locations: Article 51A(k) and Article 21A.

questions.text: A local administration proposal mixes city drainage services and district rural development. Which institutional design best reflects the course distinctions?

options.label: A
options.text: Give both tasks to the Rajya Sabha

options.label: B
options.text: Use the Municipal Corporation for urban local-government functions and the Zila Panchayat for district-level rural local government, subject to applicable state arrangements

options.label: C
options.text: Assign both to the Election Commission of India

options.label: D
options.text: Treat both as functions of the Prime Minister personally

questions.rationale: The bodies correspond to urban and rural local-government levels.

questions.text: A student must explain why constitutionalism matters when officials exercise emergency-like discretion. Which answer is strongest?

options.label: A
options.text: It means there is no separation of functions

options.label: B
options.text: It means only local bodies are bound by laws

options.label: C
options.text: It means power is structured and limited by constitutional rules, rights and institutional checks

options.label: D
options.text: It means officials may ignore law if their goal seems useful

questions.rationale: Constitutionalism prevents public power from being treated as unlimited.

questions.text: An amendment is challenged as undermining a foundational feature, but the challenger merely says the new text is different. What must the argument add?

options.label: A
options.text: A reasoned connection between the amendment's practical/legal effect and an alleged basic feature

options.label: B
options.text: Only the date it was introduced

options.label: D
options.text: The names of all members of the legislature

questions.rationale: Difference alone is not the same as destruction of a basic feature.

questions.text: A student states the Election Commission of India administers municipal elections because Article 324 concerns election control. Which constitutional arrangement resolves the point?

options.label: A
options.text: Municipal elections are outside the Constitution entirely

options.label: C
options.text: Part IXA provides a State Election Commission framework for municipality elections, while ECI handles elections assigned under Article 324

options.label: D
options.text: Lok Sabha runs municipal wards directly

questions.rationale: State Election Commissions oversee municipal elections under Article 243ZA and related provisions.

questions.text: A state policy seeks environmental improvement, but an official arbitrarily denies access to a public benefit. What is a balanced analysis?

options.label: A
options.text: Assume Article 14 applies only during elections

options.label: B
options.text: Assume Fundamental Duties erase all legal procedures

options.label: C
options.text: Treat the environmental aim as an automatic exemption from equality

options.label: D
options.text: Recognize the environmental aim and Article 51A duty, while also assessing whether the decision complies with applicable rights such as Article 14

questions.rationale: Constitutional goals and duties do not excuse arbitrary state action.

questions.text: A person cites a Directive Principle as the sole basis to demand a directly enforceable order. Which qualification should be included?

options.label: B
options.text: They guide State policy and are important in governance, but Article 37 says they are not directly enforceable by courts

options.label: C
options.text: Directive Principles are superior to every constitutional right

options.label: D
options.text: They apply only to local councils

questions.rationale: Article 37 distinguishes the principles' governance role from direct judicial enforceability.

questions.text: A constitutional issue concerns equal treatment, personal liberty and a policy directive. Which response is methodologically sound?

options.label: A
options.text: Apply only Article 51A to every dispute

options.label: B
options.text: Assume Part IV repeals Part III

options.label: C
options.text: Identify the separate questions under Article 14, Article 21 and Part IV, then interpret them together rather than treating one as automatic trump

options.label: D
options.text: Refer it to a municipal corporation as the final constitutional court

questions.rationale: Separate provisions have distinct functions and must be read coherently.

questions.text: A local government officer claims their administrative decisions are outside constitutional limits because the office is local, not national. Which principle best answers that claim?

options.label: A
options.text: Public authorities at all levels must act within applicable constitutional and legal limits

options.label: B
options.text: Constitutionalism applies only during general elections

options.label: C
options.text: Fundamental Rights apply only to Union ministers

questions.rationale: Constitutional limits are not confined to national-level institutions.
